answer_1.quote: We propose a training pipeline to build a model capable of automatically generating more plausible distractors for MCQs ...
answer_1.outputs: textual distractor options for multiple-choice questions

answer_2.quote: We evaluate the plausibility of distractors generated by our model ... using sBLEU, BERTScore, discrimination index (DI), and rank accuracy ...

answer_3.quote: We train a pairwise ranker to evaluate the relative plausibility of distractors, and use this to create the student choice dataset where distractors for each question are ranked by plausibility.

answer_4.quote: Human experts (two professors) tasked with choosing the more plausible distractor ... Human evaluation ... 15 college students evaluated the difficulty of distractors generated by our method ...
answer_4.guideline: Evaluators rated distractor quality on criteria such as difficulty, clarity, answerability, and reasoning quality using Likert scales.
